chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn 'Abdus from Muhammad ibn Zawiya from Abu 'Ali ibn Rashid who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you, you wrote to Muhammad ibn Al-Faraj teaching him that the most superior of what one recites in the obligatory [prayers] is 'Inna anzalnahu' (We revealed it) and 'Qul huwa Allahu ahad' (Say, He is Allah, One), and my chest is constricted by reciting these two during Al-Fajr [prayer].' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not let your chest be constricted by these two, for the merit, by Allah, is in these two.'

key_terms.يَضِيقُ: To constrict / feel tightness (in the chest)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas and Al-Qadr twice in Fajr prayer if it feels difficult?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) addresses a companion’s concern about the physical strain of reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas and Surah Al-Qadr twice in the Fajr prayer, a practice attributed to the Imam’s instruction to Muhammad ibn al-Faraj. The Imam reassures him that the spiritual merit (*fadl*) inherent in these chapters outweighs any perceived burden, highlighting the Shia emphasis on the profound virtue of specific Quranic surahs in daily worship. This narration underscores the balance between ritual consistency and the spiritual weight assigned to key Quranic texts in Shia devotional practice.
